subject: English
title: Priya's Mystery Adventure
hook: Help Priya understand stories by asking the right questions

slides.title: Reading Comprehension
slides.storyContext: Priya sits with her grandmother in their village home. The monsoon rain taps on the roof. Daadiji opens an old book of folktales.
slides.inSimpleWords: Learning to understand and enjoy the stories you read.

image.alt: Reading Comprehension — Reading Comprehension

slides.title: The Mystery of the Lost Parrot
slides.storyContext: One morning, Priya reads a story in her textbook: 'Karan found a colorful parrot sitting on his window. He gave it water and seeds. The next day, the parrot flew away and brought a friend. Now Karan had two parrots.'
slides.inSimpleWords: A story is like a gift—read it slowly, watch what happens, and think about why.

image.alt: The Mystery of the Lost Parrot — Reading Comprehension

slides.title: Who, What, Where, When
slides.storyContext: Daadiji asks Priya questions about the parrot story. Priya learns to spot the main details.

points.label: Who
points.text: The people or animals in the story (Karan and the parrots)

points.label: What
points.text: What happens in the story (a parrot visits, then brings a friend)

points.label: Where
points.text: Where the story takes place (on Karan's window)

points.label: When
points.text: The time of the story (morning, then next day)

slides.inSimpleWords: Always ask these 4 questions to understand any story.

image.alt: Who, What, Where, When — Reading Comprehension

slides.title: The Main Idea
slides.storyContext: Sunny barks at a lizard on the wall. Priya thinks: 'This is a small detail. The BIG idea in the parrot story is: kindness brings friendship.'

points.text: A story has a main idea—the most important thing that happens
Small details support the main idea (Karan gave water and seeds)
The main idea teaches us something (be kind to animals)

slides.inSimpleWords: The main idea is like the heart of the story; everything else supports it.

image.alt: The Main Idea — Reading Comprehension

slides.title: Finding the Order of Events
slides.storyContext: Priya uses three stones to mark: First stone (Karan finds parrot), middle stone (he gives food), last stone (parrot brings a friend). This is the order things happen.

points.text: Events happen in order: first, then, finally
Words like 'morning', 'next day', 'then' show order
Knowing the order helps you understand the story better

slides.inSimpleWords: Stories move forward like steps up a ladder—one thing after another.

image.alt: Finding the Order of Events — Reading Comprehension

slides.title: Understanding Feelings
slides.storyContext: Priya asks: 'How did Karan feel when the parrot came back with a friend?' Daadiji smiles: 'His heart was full of joy! He loved the animals even more.'

points.text: Characters have feelings (happy, sad, scared, excited)
We know their feelings from what they DO (Karan gave food = he cares)
Understanding feelings helps us like the story more

slides.inSimpleWords: Good readers feel what the characters feel.

image.alt: Understanding Feelings — Reading Comprehension

slides.title: Read and Answer
slides.storyContext: Daadiji gives Priya a short story to practice: 'Meera went to the market with her mother. She saw a stall with colorful ribbons. She chose a blue ribbon for her sister's hair. Her sister danced with joy.'

example.problem: Read the story and tell: (1) Who is the main person? (2) What did Meera do? (3) Where did it happen? (4) How did Meera's sister feel?
example.solution: (1) Meera. (2) She went to the market and bought a blue ribbon. (3) At the market. (4) Happy and joyful—she danced!

slides.inSimpleWords: Always ask WHO, WHAT, WHERE, WHEN to answer questions about stories.

image.alt: Read and Answer — Reading Comprehension

slides.title: Your Turn: Mini Story
slides.storyContext: Priya's teacher gives her a short passage: 'Ram liked to play cricket. One day, he broke the ball. He felt sad. But his friend Asha gave him a new ball. Ram was very happy. They played together until sunset.'

example.problem: Answer: (1) What was the problem? (2) How was it solved? (3) What is the main idea?
example.solution: (1) Ram broke his ball. (2) Asha gave him a new ball. (3) Real friends help when we are sad.

slides.inSimpleWords: Read carefully, ask questions, and think about what the story teaches.

image.alt: Your Turn: Mini Story — Reading Comprehension

slides.title: How to Understand Stories

points.text: Ask WHO, WHAT, WHERE, WHEN to find key details
Find the main idea—what the story is really about
Notice the order of events (first, then, finally)
Understand how characters feel
Good readers ask questions and think deeply

slides.inSimpleWords: Reading is like detective work—look for clues and understand the whole picture!

image.alt: How to Understand Stories — Reading Comprehension

subject: English
title: Anaya's Special Letters
hook: Write kind letters to friends and family the right way

characters.name: Grandpa
characters.role: lives far away in another city

slides.title: Letter Writing
slides.storyContext: Anaya's mother shows her a blue envelope. Inside is a handwritten letter from Grandpa in Delhi, asking about her school life. Anaya wants to write back.
slides.inSimpleWords: Letters are friendly messages we write by hand to someone we care about.

image.alt: Letter Writing — Letter Writing

slides.title: Why We Write Letters
slides.storyContext: Anaya learned that Grandpa's eyes get tired on his computer. A paper letter makes him very happy because he can hold it, read it slowly, and keep it forever. Her mother says: 'Your words on paper are like a warm hug.'
slides.inSimpleWords: Letters show people we care, and they treasure them.

image.alt: Why We Write Letters — Letter Writing

slides.title: Parts of a Friendly Letter
slides.storyContext: Anaya sits at the kitchen table with pencil and paper. Her mother shows her the five parts of a letter using her fingers.

points.label: Date
points.text: Write the day at the top (e.g., 15 June 2026)

points.label: Greeting
points.text: Start with 'Dear Grandpa,' or 'Hello Ria,'

points.label: Body
points.text: Tell your news and feelings (2-3 sentences)

points.label: Closing
points.text: End with 'Your loving granddaughter,' or 'With love,'

points.label: Signature
points.text: Sign your name below the closing

slides.inSimpleWords: Every letter has five parts—like a body has head, arms, and legs.

image.alt: Parts of a Friendly Letter — Letter Writing

slides.title: Writing the Date and Greeting
slides.storyContext: Anaya writes on her paper: '20 June 2026' at the top. Then she skips a line and writes: 'Dear Grandpa,'

points.text: Write today's date on the first line
Use a comma after the person's name in the greeting
Keep it warm but respectful (Dear, Hello, Hi work fine)

slides.inSimpleWords: The date and greeting welcome the reader into your letter.

image.alt: Writing the Date and Greeting — Letter Writing

slides.title: The Body: Your Message
slides.storyContext: Anaya writes: 'I hope you are well. I got 95 in my maths test today! I also played a new game at school called Tag. My friend Ria and I won our team. I miss you very much.'

points.text: Share real news from your life (school, friends, hobbies)
Use simple, clear sentences (2-4 sentences is perfect)
Tell how you feel (happy, proud, sad, excited)
Ask about the other person (How are you? What are you doing?)

slides.inSimpleWords: The body is your heart—share what matters to you.

image.alt: The Body: Your Message — Letter Writing

slides.title: The Closing and Signature
slides.storyContext: Anaya finishes writing: 'With lots of love, Anaya' at the bottom. She reads it aloud, and it sounds just right.

points.text: Choose a warm closing: 'With love,', 'Your loving...', 'All my love,'
Skip a line and write your name
Your signature shows the letter came from your heart

slides.inSimpleWords: The closing is a hug—it shows you care.

image.alt: The Closing and Signature — Letter Writing

slides.title: A Real Letter from Anaya
slides.storyContext: Here is the complete letter Anaya wrote to Grandpa.

example.problem: Write a friendly letter following all five parts.
example.solution:
20 June 2026

Dear Grandpa,

I hope you are well. I got 95 in my maths test today! I played cricket at school and scored 20 runs. I miss you so much and want you to visit soon. How are you? Are you eating well?

With lots of love,
Anaya

slides.inSimpleWords: A good letter is honest, warm, and easy to read.

image.alt: A Real Letter from Anaya — Letter Writing

slides.title: Write Your Own Letter
slides.storyContext: Ria's birthday is coming. Anaya decides to write her a birthday letter. 'I want to tell her how special she is to me,' Anaya thinks.

example.problem: Write a short friendly letter to a friend, including all five parts. Share a happy memory or tell them why they are special.
example.solution:
15 July 2026

Dear Ria,

Happy birthday to my best friend! I remember when we first met in Class 1 and we shared our lunch. Now we play together every day. You make me laugh and you are kind to everyone. I am so lucky to have you as a friend. Let's have fun at your birthday party!

With love,
Anaya

slides.inSimpleWords: When you write a letter, imagine sitting with the person and talking to them.

image.alt: Write Your Own Letter — Letter Writing

slides.title: Five Steps to Write a Letter

points.text: Write the date at the top
Use a greeting like 'Dear...' with a comma
Share real news and feelings in the body (2-4 sentences)
Close with a warm ending like 'With love,'
Sign your name—show it came from your heart

slides.inSimpleWords: Letters are love in an envelope—take time, be honest, and share your heart.

image.alt: Five Steps to Write a Letter — Letter Writing

subject: English
title: Vikram's Tale of the Clever Fox
hook: Enjoy stories full of adventure, animals, and life lessons

characters.name: Teacher Meera
characters.role: brings stories to life in class

slides.title: Story Reading
slides.storyContext: Vikram sits in the village library after school. Teacher Meera comes to him with a brown book of stories. 'Today, I have a story of a very clever fox,' she says, opening to the first page.
slides.inSimpleWords: Stories are journeys—take them with all your heart and imagination.

image.alt: Story Reading — Story Reading

slides.title: The Story Begins
slides.storyContext: Teacher Meera reads: 'Once, a hungry fox came to a village. He saw a farmer's henhouse. But the gate had a lock. How would he get inside?'
slides.inSimpleWords: Every story starts with 'once upon a time' and a problem to solve.

image.alt: The Story Begins — Story Reading

slides.title: Story Elements: Characters
slides.storyContext: Vikram learns that stories have heroes, villains, and helpers. The fox is clever and hungry. The farmer is kind but needs to protect his hens. The hens are innocent and scared.

points.text: Characters are the people and animals in the story
Main character (hero): the fox trying to solve a problem
Supporting characters: the farmer, the hens
Each character has feelings and reasons for what they do

slides.inSimpleWords: Characters are like people in real life—each one is different and special.

image.alt: Story Elements: Characters — Story Reading

slides.title: Story Elements: Plot (What Happens)
slides.storyContext: Teacher Meera shows Vikram the story's arc: Problem (fox hungry, henhouse locked) → Attempt (fox digs under the fence) → Climax (he almost gets in!) → Twist (farmer catches him!) → Ending (fox runs away and learns a lesson).

points.text: Problem: What is the challenge or trouble?
Rising Action: What does the character try? Does it work?
Climax: The most exciting or important moment
Ending: How is the problem solved? What lesson was learned?

slides.inSimpleWords: A plot is like climbing a hill—up, up, peak, then down to peace.

image.alt: Story Elements: Plot (What Happens) — Story Reading

slides.title: Story Elements: Setting (Where and When)
slides.storyContext: The fox's story happens in a village at dawn. It takes place on the outskirts of a farm, near a henhouse, under a big mango tree. The time of year is summer when foxes are hungriest.

points.text: Setting tells WHERE the story happens (village, forest, house, city)
Setting tells WHEN it happens (morning, summer, long ago, today)
The setting affects what happens (a sleepy village is different from a busy market)

slides.inSimpleWords: Setting is the stage where the story dances—it shapes everything.

image.alt: Story Elements: Setting (Where and When) — Story Reading

slides.title: The Lesson (Moral) of the Story
slides.storyContext: Vikram finishes reading and asks: 'What does this story teach us?' Teacher Meera smiles: 'The fox was clever, but being cunning doesn't always win. The farmer's honesty and kindness are stronger. Also, respecting others' things keeps you safe.'

points.text: Every good story has a lesson or moral (a teaching about life)
The lesson might be about kindness, honesty, hard work, or courage
The ending shows the lesson by what happens to the characters

slides.inSimpleWords: Every story whispers: 'This is how to live a good life.'

image.alt: The Lesson (Moral) of the Story — Story Reading

slides.title: A Complete Story for You
slides.storyContext: Teacher Meera reads Vikram a short tale: 'There was a kind boy named Arjun. He found a hungry kitten on the street. He gave it milk and rice every day. Soon, the kitten became strong and healthy. It played with Arjun and they became best friends. The whole village loved them both.'

example.problem: Find: (1) Main character? (2) Setting? (3) Problem? (4) How was it solved? (5) What is the lesson?
example.solution: (1) Arjun and the kitten. (2) The street and Arjun's home. (3) Hungry kitten, lonely Arjun. (4) Arjun fed the kitten and cared for it. (5) Kindness brings friendship and happiness.

slides.inSimpleWords: Good stories show how kind hearts change the world.

image.alt: A Complete Story for You — Story Reading

slides.title: Story Spot (Find the Elements)
slides.storyContext: Vikram reads a new short story: 'Priya lived in a small town by the river. One day, a storm came. The river flooded. Priya's neighbors were scared. She led everyone to the high ground of the old temple. All were safe. Priya became the village hero.'

example.problem: Identify: (1) Who is the hero? (2) What is the problem? (3) Where does it happen? (4) When does it happen? (5) What is the lesson?
example.solution: (1) Priya. (2) A flood from a storm. (3) A river town, at the temple. (4) During a storm/sudden crisis. (5) Courage and quick thinking save lives.

slides.inSimpleWords: Great readers spot every part of a story—characters, plot, setting, and lesson.

image.alt: Story Spot (Find the Elements) — Story Reading

slides.title: How to Enjoy Stories

points.text: Learn the characters—understand their feelings and choices
Follow the plot—beginning, middle, end, and how it's solved
Notice the setting—where and when the story happens
Find the lesson—what the story teaches about life
Use imagination—picture the story like a movie in your mind

slides.inSimpleWords: Stories are mirrors of life—read them slowly and let them speak to your heart.

image.alt: How to Enjoy Stories — Story Reading

subject: English
title: Maya's Rainbow of Words
hook: Feel the magic of poems that sing and dance

slides.title: Poetry
slides.storyContext: Rain falls on the roof of Maya's school. Poet Uncle visits Class 3 and opens a slim book of poems. 'Today, we feel with words!' he says, and reads: 'Pitter-patter, pitter-pat, raindrops dance on the mat.'
slides.inSimpleWords: Poetry is language playing music—words that sing, rhyme, and paint pictures.

image.alt: Poetry — Poetry

slides.title: Why Poets Write
slides.storyContext: Poet Uncle tells Maya: 'I write poems to catch feelings in words. When I see a butterfly, I feel free. When I hear a child laugh, I feel joy. Poems say big feelings in small, beautiful ways. A poem is a gift of the heart.'
slides.inSimpleWords: Poems let us say how we feel when words aren't enough.

image.alt: Why Poets Write — Poetry

slides.title: Rhyme: Words That Sound Alike
slides.storyContext: Poet Uncle claps and reads: 'Twinkle, twinkle, little star, How I wonder what you are!' Maya claps too—'star' and 'are' sound the same!'

points.text: Rhyme is when two words sound alike at the end (cat, bat; moon, soon)
Rhyming words make poems fun to read and easy to remember
Rhyming patterns can be AABB (first two lines rhyme, next two rhyme) or ABAB

example.problem: Find the rhyming words: 'The cat sat on a mat, She wore a funny hat.'
example.solution: sat/mat rhyme (A), hat rhymes with them too. This is AAA rhyme.

slides.inSimpleWords: Rhyme is poetry's music—when words dance to the same beat.

image.alt: Rhyme: Words That Sound Alike — Poetry

slides.title: Rhythm: The Heartbeat of Words
slides.storyContext: Poet Uncle drums on the table: 'Boom-boom-BOOM, boom-boom-BOOM. Listen to the pattern.' Maya walks to the beat, then reads a poem the same way. The words have rhythm!

points.text: Rhythm is the beat you hear when you read a poem aloud
Some syllables are strong (BOOM), some soft (boom)
Rhythm makes poems fun to say and hear

slides.inSimpleWords: Rhythm is the drum inside the poem—tap along and feel it.

image.alt: Rhythm: The Heartbeat of Words — Poetry

slides.title: Simile: Comparing Two Things
slides.storyContext: Poet Uncle reads: 'Her smile is bright like the sun.' Maya thinks: 'Oh! A smile is not really the sun, but it shines like the sun does. That's beautiful!'

points.text: A simile compares two things using 'like' or 'as'
It helps us see something in a new, beautiful way
Examples: as strong as a tiger, bright like a star, soft as cotton

example.problem: Complete the simile: 'The river flows like _____' or 'Her voice is sweet as _____'
example.solution: The river flows like a snake. Her voice is sweet as honey.

slides.inSimpleWords: Similes are word pictures—they say 'this is like that' to show beauty.

image.alt: Simile: Comparing Two Things — Poetry

slides.title: Metaphor: One Thing IS Another
slides.storyContext: Poet Uncle reads: 'Life is a journey.' Maya asks: 'But life isn't really a journey!' He smiles: 'In poetry, we can say life IS a journey because we grow and learn, just like travelers move ahead.'

points.text: A metaphor says one thing IS another (not 'like' another)
It makes us think deeply about the hidden meaning
Examples: 'Time is gold', 'Her heart is stone', 'Hope is a bird'

slides.inSimpleWords: Metaphors are magic—they make one thing become another in our minds.

image.alt: Metaphor: One Thing IS Another — Poetry

slides.title: A Poem About Rain
slides.storyContext: Poet Uncle reads a complete poem for Maya:

example.problem: Read and find: (1) Rhyming words, (2) A simile, (3) The feeling of the poem.
example.solution:
Poem: 'Pitter-patter, pat-pat-pat, rain falls like a dancing cat. Splish and splash on the ground, nature's music is the sound. Wet and cold and fresh and free, rain brings joy to you and me.'

(1) pat/cat, ground/sound, free/me rhyme.
(2) Simile: 'rain falls like a dancing cat'
(3) Joy, playfulness, and love of nature.

slides.inSimpleWords: Poetry shows us the beauty hiding in everyday things.

image.alt: A Poem About Rain — Poetry

slides.title: Write Your Own Poem
slides.storyContext: Poet Uncle gives Maya a challenge: 'Write a short poem about something you love. It can be about your pet, your home, a friend, or nature. Use rhyming words and a simile if you can!'

example.problem: Write a 4-line poem about your favorite thing. Include at least one rhyme and one simile.
example.solution: My puppy is sweet like honey on bread, She plays with me from dawn till bed. Her eyes shine bright like stars so clear, I love my puppy, she's so dear!

slides.inSimpleWords: Poets are word artists—paint feelings, rhymes, and pictures on paper.

image.alt: Write Your Own Poem — Poetry

slides.title: Poetry Magic

points.text: Rhyme makes poetry sound beautiful (words with the same ending sound)
Rhythm is the beat you feel when you read aloud
Similes compare using 'like' or 'as' (bright like a star)
Metaphors make one thing become another (life is a journey)
Poetry shows big feelings in small, beautiful words

slides.inSimpleWords: Poetry is the art of feeling with words—read it slowly, say it aloud, and let it touch your heart.

image.alt: Poetry Magic — Poetry
